editorial:
Imagine trying to fix your love life by just adding more people to the mix. That is exactly what happens here. You follow Chris, who is bored with her boyfriend Sandor and starts seeing a guy named Dennis. Things get weird fast when they all start hanging out with other people, like Jan and Phil. Before you know it, six people have decided to live together in one big group marriage. It starts off feeling like a wild social experiment with a very laid-back, 70s vibe that makes you wonder if this could actually work in real life.

The movie does a great job showing how the outside world reacts to their strange setup. You will see a lot of funny moments, but also some real tension when the media finds out and starts judging them. The acting feels natural for the time, though the pacing slows down a bit in the middle. If you enjoy stories about breaking social rules, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the best way to keep this oddity.
endingExplained: In the end, the pressure from the public and the media becomes too much for the group to handle. The dream of a six-person marriage falls apart as jealousy and outside judgment tear them apart. You see that their idealistic view of love cannot survive in a world that hates their lifestyle. Most of the group eventually splits up, proving that while the idea sounded fun, it was too complicated to actually work.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage movies about unconventional relationships.
